interest: This document illustrates Japan's cultural diplomacy and soft-power outreach toward Latin America on the eve of World War II. It reveals how Japanese educational bodies such as the Tokyo Institute of Students sought to build academic and ideological ties with South American nations by offering fully funded scholarships for sociological study. For historians, it also documents the active U.S. State Department monitoring of Japanese cultural penetration and bilateral relations within the Western Hemisphere.
overview: This file consists of a two-page consular despatch dated July 13, 1939, from American Consul Augustin W. Ferrin at Montevideo, Uruguay, approved by Consul General Dudley G. Dwyre, regarding a Japanese academic scholarship offered to Uruguay. The despatch reports that the President of Uruguay issued an executive decree on July 5, 1939 (published in the Diario Oficial on July 13), creating a jury of primary and secondary education inspectors and government council delegates to select a Uruguayan professor to study at the Tokyo Institute of Students, an international center for the study of sociological problems.

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting on an executive decree establishing a jury to select a Uruguayan professor for a scholarship at the Tokyo Institute of Students.
subfiles.summary: American Consul Augustin W. Ferrin reports on a July 5, 1939 decree by the President of Uruguay appointing a jury to select a Uruguayan professor for an educational scholarship in Japan. The scholarship was offered by the Tokyo Institute of Students, an international center for sociological study, and accepted by executive resolution on June 14, 1939. The selection jury, consisting of primary and secondary education inspectors and government delegates, was appointed to choose a successful recipient from candidates who applied by June 30, 1939.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Augustin W. Ferrin on Japanese Scholarship for Uruguayan Professor
